speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. Since you are a child with high blood pressure, I need to ask if anyone in your family has ever been diagnosed with high blood pressure or kidney disease.

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; since there is no family history, we need to investigate potential secondary causes. Do you or anyone else notice the boy having severe headaches, vision changes, or episodes of sweating and tremors? REQUEST TEST: Basic Metabolic Panel, Electrolytes, Renal Function Panel.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a very specific and concerning finding; isolated high blood pressure in one arm often suggests an obstruction in the subclavian artery or aortic arch. I will need to perform a thorough cardiovascular exam to check for a pulse deficit or a murmur. Can you tell me if you have noticed any swelling in his legs or a difference in the size of his arms? REQUEST IMAGES: Echocardiogram with Doppler flow study.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta
